- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast increase at +3% after spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract lag.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model tends to overfit recent sentiment; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
